chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from Muhammad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who said, 'I offer a camel,' and did not specify where to slaughter it, he said: 'The slaughter site is at Mina; they distribute it among the poor.' And regarding a man who said, 'I offer a camel, I will slaughter it in Kufa,' he said: 'If he specifies a place, let him slaughter it there, for it suffices for him.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A specific type of vow involving the sacrifice of a camel or other animal
key_terms.بِمِنًى: At Mina (the sacred site near Mecca)
key_terms.يُجْزِي عَنْهُ: It suffices for him (fulfills the obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one vows to sacrifice an animal but does not specify where to slaughter it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that a general vow for animal sacrifice defaults to the prophetic practice of slaughtering at Mina, reflecting the sanctity of the Hajj site. Conversely, it establishes the binding nature of specific stipulations, where naming a location like Kufa obligates the vow-maker to fulfill the sacrifice there, emphasizing the importance of intention (niyyah) and precision in fulfilling religious commitments.
